_readme: Managing authority for public access at each stocked water. Hand-maintained; never written by the scraper.
Keys match water names in stocking_data_clean.json. Run `python check_notes.py` (it validates this file too).
authority  - short display name of who manages public access (e.g. 'NM State Parks', 'Carson National Forest', 'City of Carlsbad').
category   - state_park | usfs | blm | usace | usbr | nps | usfws | nmdgf | municipal | county | university | tribal | private | mixed | unknown
unit       - the specific park / forest unit / rec area, if any.
url        - official page for that authority or unit. Prefer the specific unit page; fall back to the agency home page.
notes      - ownership vs. operation split, or for rivers, which stretches are public and who holds them. Plain text; HTML is escaped.
confidence - high | medium | low. Only high and medium are rendered on the site. Low = best guess, verify before it goes live.
source     - where the determination came from.
Rivers: 'mixed' means the reach crosses several owners including private land. Always say which stretch is public; never imply a whole river is open.

Sources used 2026-09-19: EMNRD State Parks 'Find a Park' list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ArcGIS Boat Ramps layer, Ownership field); NMDGF Rules booklet 'Regulations for Specific Waters'; agency pages found by search.

Abiquiu Reservoir.notes: Federal flood-control reservoir; recreation areas run by the Corps.
Abiquiu Reservoir.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (boat ramp ownership)

Albuquerque Drain.notes: Drains are MRGCD irrigation works; adjacent bosque trails are City of Albuquerque Open Space. Fish from the ditch banks where posted open.
Albuquerque Drain.source: NMDGF Winter Fish Stocking article; MRGCD

Albuquerque Drain (South).unit: Riverside drains, south Albuquerque (Bridge to Rio Bravo)
Albuquerque Drain (South).notes: Drains are MRGCD irrigation works; adjacent bosque trails are City of Albuquerque Open Space.
Albuquerque Drain (South).source: NMDGF Winter Fish Stocking article; MRGCD

Alto Lake.notes: Village water-supply reservoir; village boating permit required, no motors.
Alto Lake.source: NMDGF Rules booklet (city boating permit); Village of Ruidoso

Alumni Pond.notes: On the NMSU campus next to the Pan American Center.

Animas River.authority: City of Farmington / City of Aztec
Animas River.unit: Animas Park, Berg Park (Farmington); Riverside Park (Aztec)
Animas River.notes: Public access at city river parks in Farmington and Aztec; most of the river between is private.
Animas River.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramp: City of Farmington)

Bataan Lake.notes: Impoundment of the Pecos River below Lake Carlsbad.
Bataan Lake.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramp ownership); NMDGF habitat project page

Belen Riverside Drain.notes: MRGCD drain; stocked on the west bank between Los Lunas and Belen.

Berrendo Creek.notes: Creek runs through north Roswell; most frontage appears private. Verify the stocked access point.

Bill Evans Lake.unit: Bill Evans Lake (west of Silver City)
Bill Evans Lake.notes: Lake owned by the Tyrone mine (Freeport-McMoRan); public fishing managed by NMDGF under agreement. Oars or electric motors only.
Bill Evans Lake.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramp ownership); NMDGF habitat project page

Black Canyon.notes: Gila trout water; free Gila Trout Permit required. Seasonal closure above FR 150.
Black Canyon.source: NMDGF Rules booklet; Gila trout stockings from federal hatchery

Black River.notes: BLM recreation area provides the public access; much of the river elsewhere is private.

Bluewater Lake.notes: Dam and water owned by Bluewater-Toltec Irrigation District; recreation managed by State Parks.
Bluewater Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Bonito Lake.notes: Alamogordo's water-supply reservoir on Lincoln National Forest land. No boats or flotation; daylight only.
Bonito Lake.source: NMDGF Rules booklet; City of Alamogordo

Bosque Redondo.source: Village of Fort Sumner parks page

Brantley Dam.notes: Dam owned by the Bureau of Reclamation; recreation managed by State Parks.
Brantley Dam.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Brazos Lodge Pond.notes: Private lodge pond; access for guests/fee.

Brazos River.notes: Nearly all frontage is private ranch and lodge land; access is by fee or permission.

Caballo Lake.notes: Bureau of Reclamation reservoir; recreation managed by State Parks.
Caballo Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Casias Lakes.notes: Stocked from Los Ojos hatchery in 2021 only; likely private. Verify.

Cebolla River.unit: Rio Cebolla near Cebolla, Rio Arriba County
Cebolla River.notes: Stocked from Los Ojos hatchery, so this is the Rio Cebolla in Rio Arriba County, not the Jemez one. Headwaters on Carson NF; the valley is largely private.
Cebolla River.source: Hatchery source; verify the stocked access

Chama River (Abv El Vado).authority: Mixed (private / NMDGF Sargent WMA / Village of Chama)
Chama River (Abv El Vado).unit: Rio Chama above El Vado Lake
Chama River (Abv El Vado).notes: Mostly private ranch land. Public access in the Village of Chama and on NMDGF's Edward Sargent Wildlife Area.

Chama River (Below Abiquiu).notes: The ~2 miles directly below Abiquiu Dam are Corps land (NMDGF habitat project, parking added 2020). Downstream is private and pueblo land.
Chama River (Below Abiquiu).source: NMDGF Fisheries Management page (Rio Chama habitat project)

Chama River (Blw El Vado).unit: Rio Chama Wildlife Area; El Vado Ranch (private, fee)
Chama River (Blw El Vado).notes: Below the dam: El Vado Ranch (Cooper's) is private with paid access, then NMDGF's Rio Chama WMA. Further downstream is BLM/USFS Wild & Scenic river (float access, BLM permit).
Chama River (Blw El Vado).source: NMDGF Rules booklet; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramp: private-public access allowed)

Charette Lake Lower.notes: Open noon March 1 to noon Oct 31.

Cimarron River (West Of Cimarron).unit: Cimarron Canyon State Park (Colin Neblett Wildlife Area)
Cimarron River (West Of Cimarron).notes: The canyon stretch along US 64 is Cimarron Canyon State Park, on NMDGF's Colin Neblett WMA. River outside the park is private.

Clayton Lake.unit: Clayton Lake State Park & Dinosaur Trackways
Clayton Lake.notes: Open noon March 1 to noon Oct 31.
Clayton Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Cochiti Lake.unit: Cochiti Lake (on Pueblo de Cochiti land; recreation areas run by the Corps)
Cochiti Lake.notes: Flood-control reservoir operated by the Corps under lease from Pueblo de Cochiti. Cochiti and Tetilla Peak recreation areas are Corps-run; the spillway is closed to fishing and the pueblo's shoreline outside the recreation areas is closed without tribal permission.
Cochiti Lake.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramps: USACE); NMDGF Rules booklet

Comanche Creek (Lower).notes: Valle Vidal is open to fishing July 1 to Dec 31 only.

Comanche Creek (Upper).notes: Valle Vidal is open to fishing July 1 to Dec 31 only.

Conchas Lake.notes: Corps of Engineers reservoir; the Corps runs its own recreation areas and ramps near the dam, State Parks runs the rest.
Conchas Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramps: USACE)

Conoco Pond.notes: Formerly Conoco Lake. No facilities or water on site.

Corrales Riverside Drain.notes: MRGCD drain along the Corrales bosque.

Costilla Creek.authority: Mixed (Rio Costilla Cooperative Livestock Assn. / Carson National Forest)
Costilla Creek.unit: Rio Costilla Park (private, fee); Valle Vidal (USFS)
Costilla Creek.notes: Most of Costilla Creek is on private RCCLA land with day-fee access; upper reaches are in Valle Vidal (open July 1 to Dec 31).
Costilla Creek.source: NMDGF Rules booklet (Rio Costilla camping note)

Costilla River.authority: Mixed (Rio Costilla Cooperative Livestock Assn. / Carson National Forest)
Costilla River.unit: Rio Costilla Park (private, fee); Valle Vidal (USFS)
Costilla River.notes: Same water as Costilla Creek. Most frontage is private RCCLA land with day-fee access; upper reaches in Valle Vidal.
Costilla River.source: NMDGF Rules booklet (Rio Costilla camping note)

Cow Creek.notes: Stocked from Lisboa Springs (Pecos). Lower Cow Creek is largely private; headwaters are on Santa Fe NF. Verify the stocked access.

Coyote Creek (Nr Guadalupita).notes: Public access is the state park stretch; creek outside the park is private.

Eagle Nest Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Eagle Rock Lake.unit: Eagle Rock Lake Day Use Area (Questa)
Eagle Rock Lake.notes: No boating, wading or swimming (protects the lake liner).

El Porvenir Creek (2115).notes: Lower creek near the village is private.

El Rito Creek (Nr Santa Rosa).unit: El Rito Creek through Santa Rosa parks
El Rito Creek (Nr Santa Rosa).notes: Stocked from Rock Lake; creek runs through the city's park lands. Verify exact stocked stretch.

El Rito Creek (Trib Of Chama).notes: Upper creek on Carson NF; the valley through El Rito village is private.

El Vado Lake.notes: Dam owned by the Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District (Bureau of Reclamation project); recreation managed by State Parks.
El Vado Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Elephant Butte Lake.notes: Bureau of Reclamation reservoir; recreation managed by State Parks.
Elephant Butte Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Fenton Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Gallinas Ice Pond.unit: Montezuma Pond (Gallinas Canyon, near Las Vegas)
Gallinas Ice Pond.notes: The historic ice pond at Montezuma. Ownership not confirmed (United World College / City of Las Vegas area). Verify.

Gallinas River (Nr Las Vegas).authority: Mixed (City of Las Vegas / private / Santa Fe National Forest)
Gallinas River (Nr Las Vegas).unit: Gallinas River Park (city); Gallinas Canyon (USFS upstream)
Gallinas River (Nr Las Vegas).notes: Public access in Las Vegas city parks and on Santa Fe NF above Montezuma; private between.

Gila River (East, Middle, West Forks).unit: Gila Wilderness; Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument (NPS) at the forks
Gila River (East, Middle, West Forks).notes: Forks are on Gila NF / Gila Wilderness; the West Fork near the cliff dwellings is National Park Service. Gila Trout Permit required on parts of the West Fork.

Grindstone Reservoir.notes: Village boating permit required; oars/electric only; trolling speed.

Guadalupe River.notes: Rio Grande cutthroat stockings from Seven Springs; this is the Rio Guadalupe in the Jemez, not a Guadalupe County water (site coordinates are wrong).
Guadalupe River.source: Hatchery source; NMDGF Rules booklet (Rio Guadalupe Special Trout Water)

Harris Lake.source: NMDGF Rules booklet (Harris Pond, Las Vegas)

Harry Mcadams Park Pond.notes: Former state park, now city-run. Kids/seniors/disabled anglers only.

Heron Reservoir.notes: Bureau of Reclamation reservoir; recreation managed by State Parks. No-wake lake.
Heron Reservoir.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Hidden Lake (Aka Lake Hazel).notes: Backcountry lake stocked only with Rio Grande cutthroat fingerlings, like the neighboring Trampas Lakes. Identified by GNIS as the Hidden Lake beside Trampas Lakes; the Lake Hazel alias is unconfirmed.

Hondo River (Lower).unit: Rio Hondo below Arroyo Hondo (Rio Grande del Norte NM)
Hondo River (Lower).notes: The lowest reach to the Rio Grande (John Dunn Bridge area) is BLM; the valley through Arroyo Hondo and Valdez is private.

Horseshoe Lake.notes: Rio Grande cutthroat water reached by trail from the Middle Fork/Lost Lake trailhead. Site coordinates are wrong (they point near Carlsbad).

Jemez River.unit: Jemez Ranger District (NM 4 above Jemez Springs)
Jemez River.notes: Public water is the Santa Fe NF stretch along NM 4 above Jemez Springs (Battleship Rock, Dark Canyon, etc.). Through Jemez Springs it is private; below Cañon it is Pueblo of Jemez land and closed without a pueblo permit.

Jemez River East Fork.unit: Jemez Ranger District (Las Conchas, Jemez Falls); Valles Caldera National Preserve upstream
Jemez River East Fork.notes: Lower East Fork along NM 4 is Santa Fe NF. Inside Valles Caldera it is National Park Service with its own fishing permit.

Joe Vigil Lake.notes: Backcountry lake at ~11,700 ft near Truchas Peaks; Rio Grande cutthroat water.
Joe Vigil Lake.source: USGS name (Jose Vigil Lake); hatchery source

Laguna Del Campo (Burns Lake).notes: Open May 1 to Oct 31; kids 14 and under with up to two supervising adults, seniors, and anglers with disabilities.

Lake Alice (Sugarite Canyon).notes: Oars or electric motors only; daylight hours.
Lake Alice (Sugarite Canyon).source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Rules booklet

Lake Farmington.notes: City water-supply lake; non-motorized craft only in season.

Lake Katherine.notes: Backcountry lake below Santa Fe Baldy.

Lake Maloya.notes: City of Raton water-supply reservoir; recreation managed by State Parks. Oars or electric only.
Lake Maloya.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Lake Roberts.notes: Oars or electric motors only; trolling speed.

Lake Roberts Glenwood Trout Hatchery.notes: Data artifact: a hatchery name leaked into the water-name column. Not a real water.

Lake Sumner.notes: Bureau of Reclamation reservoir; recreation managed by State Parks.
Lake Sumner.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Lake Van.notes: Town-run lake park with camping. (Town has no reliable website; call 575-734-5482.)
Lake Van.source: Lake Van Park listings (Town of Dexter operated)

Leandro Creek.notes: Stocked from Los Ojos hatchery (Chama area). Ownership not confirmed; may be private ranch land. Verify.

Los Pinos River.authority: Mixed (NMDGF Rio de los Pinos WMA / Carson National Forest / private)
Los Pinos River.unit: Rio de los Pinos Wildlife Area
Los Pinos River.notes: Public access on NMDGF's Rio de los Pinos WMA and Carson NF; private ranch land between.
Los Pinos River.source: NMDGF Rules booklet (Rio de los Pinos Special Trout Water)

Lower Trampas (Aka Lake Ruth).notes: Backcountry lake reached from the Trampas Lakes trailhead.

Manzano Lake.notes: Small pond in the village of Manzano; last stocked 2020. Ownership (land grant / private) not confirmed.

Maxwell Lake 13.notes: Open noon March 1 to Oct 31; trolling speed. Ramp often dry at low water.

Middle Fork Lake.notes: 4WD road or hike from the Middle Fork trailhead.

Monastery Lake.notes: Daylight only; no boats or flotation; no ice fishing.

Mora (Pecos River Drainage).unit: Pecos Canyon State Park (Mora Campground area)
Mora (Pecos River Drainage).notes: Rio Mora at its confluence with the Pecos is in Pecos Canyon State Park; upstream is Santa Fe NF.

Morphy Reservoir.notes: Open March 1 to Oct 31; oars or electric only.
Morphy Reservoir.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Mt View Ponds (Aka Cowles Ponds).notes: Smaller pond is kids/seniors/disabled anglers only.

Navajo Reservoir.notes: Bureau of Reclamation reservoir; recreation managed by State Parks.
Navajo Reservoir.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Pecos River (Cowles To Village Of Pecos).unit: Pecos Canyon State Park (Dalton, Bert Clancey, Mora, Terrero, Cowles day-use areas)
Pecos River (Cowles To Village Of Pecos).notes: Public access is at the Pecos Canyon State Park units and Santa Fe NF campgrounds along NM 63; much of the canyon between them is private and posted.

Pecos River (I-40 To Lake Sumner).unit: Santa Rosa Lake State Park; Puerto de Luna area
Pecos River (I-40 To Lake Sumner).notes: Mostly private ranch land. Public access at Santa Rosa Lake State Park and in Santa Rosa city parks.

Pecos River (Lake Sumner To Roswell).unit: Sumner Lake State Park (below dam / stilling basin)
Pecos River (Lake Sumner To Roswell).notes: The stilling basin and tailwater below Sumner Dam are in the state park (Winter Trout Water). Downstream to Roswell is almost entirely private.
Pecos River (Lake Sumner To Roswell).source: NMDGF Rules booklet (Sumner Lake stilling basin)

Pecos River (Pecos Canyon).unit: Pecos Canyon State Park; Santa Fe NF above Cowles
Pecos River (Pecos Canyon).notes: Public access at Pecos Canyon State Park units and Santa Fe NF (Jacks Creek, Iron Gate, Pecos Wilderness) above Cowles. Private inholdings between are posted.

Pecos River (Vill Of Pecos - Villanueva).notes: Mostly private through the villages; reliable public access is Villanueva State Park at the bottom of the reach, plus NMDGF's Monastery Lake stretch near Pecos.
Pecos River (Vill Of Pecos - Villanueva).source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Rules booklet

Pecos River (Villanueva To I-40).notes: Villanueva State Park at the top of the reach is the public access; below it the river is private ranch land.

Peralta Drain.unit: Peralta drain (east bank), Los Lunas to Belen
Peralta Drain.notes: MRGCD drain; stocked on the east bank between Los Lunas and Belen.

Quemado Lake.notes: Recreation area is Gila NF (Quemado RD); NMDGF built the dam and owns the boat ramp. Oars or electric only.
Quemado Lake.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramp: NMDGF); USFS

Rancho Grande Pond.unit: Rancho Grande Estates, west of Reserve
Rancho Grande Pond.notes: Private subdivision ponds opened to public fishing under an NMDGF agreement.

Red River (Abv Questa).authority: Mixed (Town of Red River / Carson National Forest / NMDGF)
Red River (Abv Questa).unit: Carson NF campgrounds (Junebug, Elephant Rock, Fawn Lakes); Town of Red River; NMDGF Red River Hatchery
Red River (Abv Questa).notes: Above town: Carson NF. In town: Town of Red River parks. Between town and Questa: Carson NF campgrounds along NM 38, then the Chevron mine (private, closed) and the NMDGF hatchery.

Red River (Below Questa).unit: Wild Rivers Recreation Area (Rio Grande del Norte National Monument); NMDGF Red River Hatchery
Red River (Below Questa).notes: From the hatchery down through the gorge is BLM; private land around Questa.

Red River City Ponds.notes: Open March 1 to Nov 15; middle pond is kids/seniors/disabled only.

Rio Bonito Lower.unit: Fort Stanton-Snowy River Cave National Conservation Area
Rio Bonito Lower.notes: Public stretch runs through BLM's Fort Stanton NCA; through Lincoln and below it is private.

Rio Grande (Elephant Butte To Caballo).authority: Mixed (NM State Parks / Bureau of Reclamation / private)
Rio Grande (Elephant Butte To Caballo).unit: Elephant Butte Lake SP (Dam Site); Caballo Lake SP
Rio Grande (Elephant Butte To Caballo).notes: Tailwater below Elephant Butte Dam is Reclamation land in the state park; the reach through Truth or Consequences has city river parks; much of the rest is private. Winter Trout Water.

Rio Grande (Gorge- Abv Pilar).unit: Rio Grande del Norte National Monument (Orilla Verde, Wild Rivers, John Dunn Bridge)

Rio Grande (Pilar To Cochiti Lake).authority: Mixed (Bureau of Land Management / private / pueblo)
Rio Grande (Pilar To Cochiti Lake).unit: Orilla Verde Recreation Area (Pilar to Taos Junction Bridge)
Rio Grande (Pilar To Cochiti Lake).notes: BLM from Pilar down through the Racecourse and Orilla Verde; private through Embudo and Velarde; Ohkay Owingeh, Santa Clara, San Ildefonso and Cochiti pueblo lands below Española are closed without tribal permission.

Rio Las Vacas.unit: Cuba Ranger District (Rio de las Vacas Campground)

Rio Pueblo.authority: Mixed (Carson National Forest / private / Picuris Pueblo)
Rio Pueblo.unit: Camino Real Ranger District (Sipapu to Tres Ritos)
Rio Pueblo.notes: Public water is the Carson NF stretch along NM 518 above Vadito; through Peñasco it is private and Picuris Pueblo.

Rito De Los Pinos.notes: The Rito de los Pinos in Sandoval County near Cuba (GNIS), stocked from Los Ojos.
Rito De Los Pinos.source: GNIS (Sandoval Co.); existing site coordinates agree

Rock Lake Hatchery Kids Ponds (Near Rosw.notes: Anglers 11 and younger only; 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (The hatchery is at Santa Rosa, not Roswell.)

Ruidoso River.authority: Mixed (Village of Ruidoso / private / Mescalero Apache Tribe)
Ruidoso River.unit: Two Rivers Park and other village river parks
Ruidoso River.notes: Public access at Village of Ruidoso river parks; upstream is Mescalero Apache tribal land (closed), and most other frontage is private.

San Antonio River.unit: Jemez Ranger District (San Antonio Campground); Valles Caldera upstream
San Antonio River.notes: Santa Fe NF along NM 126; inside Valles Caldera it is National Park Service with its own permit.

San Gregorio Lake.notes: Short hike in; boats without motors only.

San Juan River (Blw Quality).notes: State park access continues below the Quality Water boundary; further downstream toward Hammond is mostly private.
San Juan River (Blw Quality).source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramps: NM State Parks)

San Juan River (Quality).unit: Navajo Lake State Park (Quality Waters below Navajo Dam)
San Juan River (Quality).notes: The Quality Water stretch is within Navajo Lake State Park on Bureau of Reclamation land; NMDGF sets the special regulations.
San Juan River (Quality).source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Santa Cruz Reservoir.notes: Water owned by the Santa Cruz Irrigation District; recreation area managed by BLM Taos Field Office. Limited days/hours (see rules).

Santa Rosa Lake.notes: Corps of Engineers reservoir; recreation managed by State Parks.
Santa Rosa Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Seven Springs Brood Pond.notes: Anglers 11 and younger only; 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Shuree Ponds.notes: Open July 1 to Dec 31; one pond is kids only; no motors.

Sipapu Pond.notes: Resort pond open to the public.

Springer Lake.authority: NM Dept. of Game & Fish (Open Gate)
Springer Lake.notes: Town of Springer reservoir; public fishing access through NMDGF's Open Gate program. No ice fishing.
Springer Lake.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramp: NMDGF-Open Gate)

Storrie Reservoir.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Stubblefield Lake.authority: NM Dept. of Game & Fish (Open Gate)
Stubblefield Lake.notes: Irrigation reservoir adjacent to Maxwell NWR; public access through NMDGF's Open Gate program. Often dry.
Stubblefield Lake.source: NMDGF Fishing Waters Map (ramp: NMDGF-Open Gate)

Tajique Creek.notes: Public water is on Cibola NF above Tajique village.

Taos Creek (Aka Rio Fernando De Taos).notes: Carson NF through Taos Canyon; private through the town of Taos.

Timberon Ponds.notes: Stocked by a private vendor per NMDGF reports. Summer Catfish Water.
Timberon Ponds.source: NMDGF Rules booklet; stocking hatchery field = Private

Trees Lake.source: NMDGF Rules booklet; Deming tourism page

Upper Trampas (Aka Lake Alice).notes: Backcountry lake reached from the Trampas Lakes trailhead.

Ute Lake.source: EMNRD State Parks list; NMDGF Fishing Waters Map

Willow Creek (Pecos Drainage).unit: Pecos Canyon State Park (Willow Creek area)
Willow Creek (Pecos Drainage).notes: Confluence area is in Pecos Canyon State Park; upstream is Santa Fe NF.
